placeholderNote: Rebuilt from our Jul 13 call - your pricing, your guarantee, your objection answers, in your words. Anything you disagree with, change it here. The sample leads below are REAL Atlanta-area businesses, and we didn't guess at their size: every one filed a Form 5500 with the Department of Labor showing $300k-$400k a year going into staff retirement plans. That's public, verifiable proof they clear your $1M floor - better than any database estimate. There are 637 more like them in Atlanta metro and 1,319 in Georgia. Rate these 1-5 and tell us which VERTICALS to lean into - that's the one decision we can't make for you.

icps.label: The core filter (what we launch with)

fields.companySize: $1M-$10M revenue. Below $1M the engagement can't clear 25% of their bottom line - that's your math, and it's the floor. $20M+ is possible but you called it a harder sale. High-margin businesses only: they have to be able to hand over $3k-$5k/mo and not feel it.
countries: United States - Georgia first, then Southeast, then East Coast, then national
signals: None required - if they fit the model, they're a lead. We start broad and tighten around whoever replies.

fields.companySize: $2M-$20M in settlements. Contingency-fee firms: they front case costs for years and get paid in huge unpredictable lumps. That's a cash-flow problem run by litigators.
countries: United States - Atlanta is a heavy PI market

fields.companySize: $1M-$10M. NOT general dental - the median single-location practice sits at or under your floor. Specialty and cash-pay clear it easily: oral surgery, perio, ortho, plastics, med spa, dermatology, fertility, LASIK.

icps.label: Candidate: The 'PE is coming for you' cluster

fields.companySize: $2M-$10M. Specialty trades (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing - NOT general contracting), independent insurance agencies, MSPs. All in active roll-up markets. Their exit multiple depends on financials that survive diligence, and most get marked down because the books are a mess.

doNotTarget: Restaurants - razor-thin margins, your call. Bookkeeping at most, never CFO.
Anything thin-margin: retail, grocery, distribution/wholesale, general contracting, staffing, trucking. Same reason as restaurants - $5M of revenue at a 5% margin can't fund a $60k engagement.
Under $1M revenue - these are bookkeeping leads, not CFO leads. We'll hold them in a separate bucket rather than throw them away.
Far from you geographically, until we've proven the close rate closer to home. You flagged this: a prospect in Alaska or Minnesota tends to want someone local.

services.name: Tax Planning
services.line: Would you rather hand the IRS $50,000, or hand us $20,000 and keep $30,000? Typical plan runs $8k-$10k, up to $50k-$60k on complex work.

services.name: Virtual CFO / FP&A
services.line: Not two pieces of paper a month you can't read - financial dashboards, advanced analytics, and a written narrative that tells you what to actually do. Starts at $5,000/mo.

services.name: Accounting / Bookkeeping
services.line: Held back from this campaign on purpose - too low-value for cold outreach. Sub-$1M replies get parked here for a later campaign.

guarantees: If the tax plan doesn't save you at least 2x what you paid for it, you're fully refunded. You can tell before accepting an engagement whether that's achievable, which is why you can afford to offer it.
If we double your investment, you win. If we don't, you get financial insight AND your money back. Either way you're up.
problemsSolved: You're getting bland financial statements from a low-end bookkeeper - blank categories, nothing you can actually act on. You might as well be doing it yourself.
Your accountant reports what already happened. Nobody is telling you what to do next, or what it's worth.
You're overpaying the IRS because nobody planned - they just filed.
proof: A client doing $23M/year: we found $1.5M in savings in the first two months. That's not even the tax side. (NEED YOUR OK TO USE THIS - it's the strongest number you have.)
We build the same investor-ready reporting for a personal injury firm that's recovered $100M+ in settlements.
Multi-state, spiky-income returns for pro athletes and one of the largest law firms in Texas.
100+ five-star Google reviews (you corrected us on this - please confirm the number you want us to claim).
offer.guidingQuestion: What is the MECHANISM? 'Double your money or your money back' is a claim everyone in this market makes. What do you actually DO that lets you promise it safely - and that your competitors don't? That sentence is the campaign.
offer.frontEndOffer: The call itself. Your offer is a no-brainer, so there's nothing left to give away first - and if someone won't take a 15-minute call for a zero-risk offer, they were never going to buy. We ask for the call directly.
leadMagnets: DECIDED: no lead magnet at launch. The guarantee IS the offer, and it's stronger than any PDF we could send.

We deliberately will NOT send the dashboard report cold - that's your differentiator, and a prospect who receives it can hand it straight to their current accountant. We describe WHAT it is, never HOW it's built.
Holding in reserve if the offer underperforms: the dashboard marketing pages you offered to build (a link beats an attachment - attachments hurt deliverability), and your existing one-pager.

emails.subject: {{company}} + the IRS
emails.body:
{{first_name}} - if you owe the IRS $50k, would you rather pay them $50k, or pay us $20k and keep $30k?

We model the plan before we ever accept the engagement, which is why we can say this: if it doesn't find at least 2x its own fee, you're fully refunded.

Worth 15 minutes to run your numbers?

emails.subject: before year-end
emails.body:
{{first_name}} - most accountants file. They don't plan. So they show up in April and report what already happened, and every move that could have cut your bill expired months ago.

We do it the other way round: we model entity structure, comp split, retirement and depreciation BEFORE the deadlines, and we run that model before we take you on. That's why we can guarantee it - if the plan doesn't find 2x its own fee in savings, you don't pay for it.

Most of what's left for this tax year has to be executed before Dec 31, not discovered in April.

Open to a quick call to run the numbers?

emails.subject: your monthly financials
emails.body:
{{first_name}} - quick one. When your books land each month, do they actually tell you what to do next, or is it two pages of categories you have to interpret yourself?

We do the accounting, then we add the part almost nobody does: dashboards, analytics, and a written narrative on what the numbers mean. One client at $23M found $1.5M in savings in the first two months - and that was before we touched their taxes.

Worth a look at what yours would show?

items.a: Never ignore it - acknowledge it first, because if you ignore that, they'll assume you'd ignore them as a client. Then reframe: we're here to give you a second opinion. Does your current accounting team offer FP&A - intuitive financial dashboards that help you make informed decisions? Investor-ready reports? Your words: the conversion rate on that reframe is high.
items.ask: This is captured from the call - did we get it right?

You didn't name a vertical, and you told us to lean on our expertise. But prospects WILL ask. Do you want to be positioned as generalists who go deep on the numbers, or should we lead with a specific industry you've served? (Your PI law firm client is the strongest single story you have.)

items.a: A rarity as an objection. A firm our size, with our review count - they know we have CPAs and EAs on staff.
items.ask: Confirming so copy claims exactly what's true: we will say the FIRM has CPAs and EAs. We will not make any claim about a specific individual's licence unless you tell us to. Good?

items.a: Our costs are based on your bottom line - our number one goal is protecting it. Every business is different, so get on a call, we'll understand yours end to end, and we'll give you a live quote right there. (Your line: nine times out of ten, we close them.)
items.ask: Captured from the call. Confirm we never state a price in an email?

items.q: "Is a tax firm even allowed to email me like this?"
items.ask: You know these rules far better than we do. Anything we must say, or must never say, in an email going out under your name?

risks.risk: Lead quality in weeks 1-3 - the one that decides everything
risks.prevention: You told us quality is the whole game, so we're building the check in from day one: every interested reply gets validated against revenue and margin BEFORE it reaches your calendar. But we need your feedback fast. If a lead is wrong, we have to hear it in week one, not month two - by month two the campaign has already been tuned around the wrong signal.

risks.risk: We don't know your industry yet
risks.prevention: You told us to lean on our expertise, so we go deliberately BROAD at launch and tighten around whoever actually replies. Narrowing to a vertical before we have data would be guessing. Your 5-10 examples are what shortcut this.

Monitored daily, with warm-up buffers and rotation. Google and Microsoft change their filters every few months; when it happens it's usually a two-week dip. You'll hear it from us first, with the fix attached.

risks.risk: A cold lead is not a referral
risks.prevention: You close nine out of ten - on referrals, where trust is already there. A cold prospect arrives colder and asks harder questions. We'll send a one-pager before every meeting so your closer knows the revenue and the pain points before they dial, which is exactly what you asked for.

expectations.greatMeeting: The decision-maker on the call (you said 9/10 they show up when money is the topic), their revenue understood before it starts, and their pain points already known - so your closer knows what to hit. Pre-qualified, ready to close, not asking beginner questions.

openQuestions.q: What is your MECHANISM? What do you actually do that lets you guarantee 2x safely, when your competitors can't?
openQuestions.why: Biggest one on this page. A guarantee with no mechanism behind it reads as a claim anyone could make, and it gets ignored. The mechanism is what makes it believable - and it's the one thing we can't write for you.

openQuestions.q: Your 5-10 ideal clients - just websites or company names.
openQuestions.why: You told us to pick the industry. These examples ARE the spec: we reverse-engineer the pattern from your best clients and the whole list sharpens. Nothing else replaces this.

openQuestions.q: Who do you NOT want to hear from, beyond restaurants?
openQuestions.why: Anti-patterns cut a bad list faster than any filter we can invent.

openQuestions.q: Which page should our sending domains point to?
openQuestions.why: They're warming now and forward to vibefinancials.com. Heads up: the Outsourced CFO Services page is still showing placeholder text ('Lorem ipsum'). A prospect who gets curious will click. Either we point somewhere else, or that page gets finished before Jul 27.

openQuestions.q: Can we use the $23M client / $1.5M-in-two-months number in cold emails, even anonymised?
openQuestions.why: It's the strongest proof you have and it makes the CFO angle concrete. We won't use it without your explicit yes.

openQuestions.q: The dashboard marketing pages you offered to build, plus your existing one-pager.
openQuestions.why: Backup if the offer alone underperforms. A link beats an attachment - attachments hurt deliverability.

openQuestions.q: An email address under vibefinancials.com for us, and access to the Teams channel.
openQuestions.why: So every reply is visible to your team from day one, and a prospect question that only you can answer doesn't sit for a day.

openQuestions.q: The booking link meetings should land on, and who's taking them.
openQuestions.why: You said accountants and closers, not one person. We need the calendar wired before launch.

openQuestions.q: The Google reviews link - you said 100+, our crawl found 55.
openQuestions.why: We want to claim a number you can point at if a prospect checks.
